findings: The registered local PDF is arXiv:2305.00164v2, stamped 10 March 2024, by T. Tony Cai, Ran Chen and Yuancheng Zhu. Its title, 26-page length and SHA-256 agree with the original pinned audit. No journal-version substitution was made.

Independent enumeration finds eleven actual Theorem environments: 2.1 on page 6; 2.2 on page 9; 2.3 on page 10; 3.1-3.4 on page 16; and 4.1-4.4 on page 23. All complete original statements were visually compared with registered-PDF renders. Theorem citations and Propositions were excluded. Section 5 ends on page 25, followed by acknowledgments, a pointer to a separate supplement and references ending on page 26. No supplementary body was read.

Theorem 2.1 retains all four local-modulus comparisons, epsilon/3 in the confidence lower bounds, and all four constant values. Theorem 2.2 retains the strict upper bounds 274 epsilon squared and 3^7 (1-2 alpha)^3 epsilon squared. Theorem 2.3 retains both estimator cases and their distinct constants 1/40 and 1/8; its printed gamma<0.1 is not changed, while the positive-gamma context is separately preserved from Remark 2.3.

Theorems 3.1-3.4 retain the exact constants 53, 449 and (24 times 2^K_alpha minus 3) times 17.5, all coverage assertions, and the original location of the alpha restriction in Theorem 3.4. Theorems 4.1-4.4 retain the discrete-design benchmarks and their own estimator/interval references. No positivity is added for C3 in Theorem 4.3 and no omitted target phrase is inserted into Theorem 4.4.

All 37 source entries and four auxiliary passages were checked. The class consists of convex functions on [0,1] with a unique minimizer; no differentiability or positive second derivative is imposed. Risk benchmarks retain sup_g inf_estimator max_h ordering. Confidence-length benchmarks require coverage on {f,g} but evaluate expected length at f alone. Continuous L2 moduli and water-filling quantities are kept distinct from discrete regression benchmarks.

The white-noise construction retains its three independent Gaussian copies, dyadic localization, remote stopping contrasts, midpoint estimator, shifted minimum estimator, both interval windows and Gaussian-maximum calibration. The source prints an ordinary integral of Y_e(t) dt for bar-X and mixed hatted/unhatted j indices in the shift. These are preserved, with unresolved-domain and coarse-level count issues recorded separately.

The regression construction retains n+1 observations at indices 0 through n, known sigma, Gaussian augmentation and infinity extension. Its block-count denominator 2^(J-j-1) differs from the localization cap denominator 2^(J-j); both printed formulas are preserved. The omitted observation zero in the extra-noise independence sentence, partial final blocks, and absent general small-n/argmin conventions remain explicit source notes.

Both regression endpoint algorithms were visually checked in full. Algorithm 1 applies only when no threshold fires and the horizon J forces termination. Algorithm 2 applies only when the desired fine level exceeds J. Their boundary cases, noisy slope conditions, ratios, clipping operations and final intervals are retained. The right linear function in Algorithm 2 omits its explicit argument on the defining left-hand side in the source; this notation is preserved.

All 45 direct theorem uses and the recursive local dependency reasons were reviewed, yielding 100 related-theorem connections. White-noise procedures do not reach regression theorems. Regression procedures do not reach white-noise theorems. Shared Gaussian quantiles and calibration constants do not import either observation model. Theorem 2.3 has arbitrary estimators and no dependency on the later adaptive procedures; the local moduli reach only Theorem 2.1.

All natural-language names, source keywords, naming contexts and highlight selectors were checked against their source passages, including the Sample Splitting heading on page 11. Four saved naming contexts, D6, D7, D9 and D10, contained control characters produced by interpreted Python escapes for alpha, rho and varepsilon. Their PDF notation was restored in the extraction script and all four derived JSON artifacts. The theorem inventory, original interface statements, dependency graph, names and selectors are unchanged.

Previous root JSON artifacts and scripts were archived before repair. A recursive comparison confirms exactly sixteen string changes: the four corrected naming contexts in each of source-passages.json, interface-draft.json, unfinalized-census.json and ranked-interfaces.json. source-transcription-corrections.json and evidence/revalidation/artifact-delta.json preserve the before/after evidence.

The per-paper scripts now write only through main entry points. The inventory writer verifies the registered local PDF instead of depending on an external source location. scripts/rebuild.py reproduced all six saved census artifacts byte for byte in an empty directory, without rewriting source-review records. Separate validator processes pass the inventory and final census. These checks certify provenance and internal consistency; the source review does not certify proofs.
